summary: An L-4 groundhouse built in the 1950s (replacing a 1931 cab) in Washington's Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, famous for reporting the 1994 Tyee Fire; now a rough-access volunteer-maintained rental, closed for 2026 due to nearby wildfires.

facts.design: Hip-roof L-4, 14x14 ft (NHLR) / listed as 16x16 ft cabin (Recreation.gov) groundhouse with catwalk
facts.status_note: Volunteer-maintained; lightning protection reported out of code as of 2013, with no funded plan to restore fire-watch use; closed for remainder of 2026 season due to nearby wildfires

access.note: Forest Service rental via Recreation.gov, but requires 4WD high-clearance vehicle or ~4-mile hike; closed for 2026 season due to wildfires

visit.trail_note: Final 3.6 miles of access road (FS 5713) are narrow, steep, sandy, with two rock ledges; alternative is a roughly 4-mile walk

events.note: An earlier L-4 cab on the same site, per firelookout.com
NHLR dates the current hip-roof L-4 groundhouse to 1952
Tyee Fire started as a lightning strike reported by the lookout; burned ~180,000 acres over weeks, destroyed 22 homes and the lookout's outhouse
Entiat RD Fire Management Officer reported lightning protection system out of code; no budget to upgrade, no plans to use Tyee for fire detection (per Feb 8, 2013 report by Ken Jones)
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 1, 1995

evidence.supports: built 1952, hip-roof L-4 14x14 groundhouse with catwalk, built by Wenatchee National Forest
evidence.quote: The hip-roof L-4 14' x 14' groundhouse with catwalk was built in 1952 by the Wenatchee Nat. Forest.

evidence.supports: 1994 Tyee Fire reported as small lightning strike, grew to 180,000 acres, destroyed 22 homes and the outhouse
evidence.quote: The Tyee Mountain Lookout made national headlines in the summer of 1994 when it reported the devastating Tyee Fire as a small lightning strike. The fire burned for weeks (180,000 acres) and the damage included 22 homes and the Tyee outhouse.

evidence.supports: 2013 report that lightning protection system is out of code, no budget, no plans to use for fire detection
evidence.quote: I have been advised by the Entiat RD Fire Mgmt Officer that Tyee LO can not be used, even by volunteers, because the lightning protection system is apparently not up to code. Cost to upgrade the system would be several thousand dollars, which isn't in their budgets. Therefore, there are no plans to utilize Tyee in the foreseeable future.

evidence.supports: earlier 1931 L-4 cab on the same site, replaced in the 1950s, threatened by 1994 Tyee-Hatchery Fire, currently a recreation rental on the NHLR, Wenatchee National Forest
evidence.quote: This ground-mounted L-4 cab, which replaced an earlier 1931 L-4 cab, was built in the 1950's. It was threatened by the massive Tyee-Hatchery Fire in 1994 (the outhouse was burnt to a crisp). It is presently available as a Recreation Rental, and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: elevation 6,654 ft, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, used by Forest Service personnel until the 1990s
evidence.quote: The Tyee Lookout sits at an elevation of 6,654 feet in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. Built in the 1950's, the lookout was used by Forest Service personnel until the 1990's.

evidence.supports: rough access road requiring 4WD high-clearance, final 3.6 miles narrow/steep/sandy with two rock ledges, or ~4 mile walk
evidence.quote: Starting with the access road, the lookout is accessible by four-wheel drive truck from mid-June to mid-October. The last 3.6 miles of the road are narrow, steep, sandy and very rocky; including two rock ledges, good tires are a must. ... As an alternative to driving, the lookout is accessible by walking the last 4 miles up the road.

evidence.supports: 16x16 cabin sleeps four on foam mattresses
evidence.quote: The 16x16 cabin sleeps four and is equipped with four single foam mattresses, two on regular frames and two on trundle style frames.

evidence.supports: closed for remainder of 2026 season due to wildfires
evidence.quote: Tyee Lookout will be closed for the remainder of the 2026 season due to wildfires in the area. Reservation-holders will receive an email with additional information.

evidence.supports: steep drop-offs on two sides, rocky uneven ground
evidence.quote: Sitting at the top of the mountain, the wind blows frequently... Two sides of the lookout drop off very steep to the valley below, a fall would be bad, keep kids away from the edge.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1952 for the current structure; firelookout.com says 'the 1950's' and notes it replaced an earlier 1931 L-4 cab on the same site. The brief's conflict note (differing build years) is explained by one source dating the current structure and another potentially conflating it with the original 1931 cab; kept both in the story as a stated disagreement rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: Cabin dimensions conflict slightly: NHLR says 14x14 ft, Recreation.gov's current listing says 16x16 ft -- could reflect a later rebuild/remodel or simple inconsistency; reported both without resolving. Height_m omitted: no source gave a tower/cab height figure (it's a low groundhouse, brief gave no height_m either). Access level recorded as 'public' via paid rental, but note the 2013 report on lightning-protection non-compliance and the active 2026 wildfire closure -- actual availability fluctuates and should be checked against current Recreation.gov status before publishing anything time-sensitive. Fact-check 2026-10-04: elevation also conflicts across sources -- NHLR itself states 6,511 ft, while firelookout.com and Recreation.gov both state 6,654 ft. The story's opening sentence cited NHLR for the 6,654 figure it does not support; citation corrected to firelookout.com + Recreation.gov (the two sources that actually give that number).
